key_insight: The paper shows that large language models contain highly specialized, low-overlap functional subnetworks that can be selectively updated to reduce catastrophic forgetting in continual learning.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to make LLM adaptation more parameter- and memory-efficient by restricting training and optimizer updates to task-specific regions of the model.
method: Use gradient-attribution profiling to identify cognition-associated subnetworks with minimal mutual overlap.
Route each incoming training example to its corresponding functional subnetwork.
Apply Function-isolated Memory-Efficient Optimization (CiMEO) to limit parameter updates and optimizer states to selected regions.
evidence_signal: On 1.4 million sequential instructions, CiMEO achieved the best average performance across five generative benchmarks covering programming, examination-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning while reducing forgetting.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliably localizing and routing tasks to the right subnetworks, which may be challenging when task boundaries are ambiguous or distributions shift.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
